routes.why: The official termination notice is a written document and can establish that the termination was communicated in writing.
The official termination form can identify whether the prescribed canton-approved form was used.
The termination form can be examined for the required information on challenging the termination and requesting a tenancy extension.
A marriage certificate establishes that the tenant had a spouse at the relevant time.
Household registration can establish the tenant's recorded household and registered-partnership status at the time of termination.
The separately addressed notice, envelope, and registered-mail receipt, read with proof of marriage, can show service on the tenant separately from the spouse.
The separately addressed notice, envelope, and registered-mail receipt, read with household-registration evidence, can show service on the tenant separately from a registered partner.
The separately addressed notice, envelope, and registered-mail receipt, read with proof of marriage, can show service on the spouse separately from the tenant.
The separately addressed notice, envelope, and registered-mail receipt, read with household-registration evidence, can show service on a registered partner separately from the tenant.
These documents permit assessment of the prescribed form, required notice content, and separate service on married tenants, and can reveal a formal defect under Articles 266l–266n.

These documents permit assessment of the prescribed form, required notice content, and separate service where the tenant has a registered partner, and can reveal a formal defect under Articles 266l–266n.
Landlord correspondence can evidence the landlord's stated reasons, motive, or retaliatory conduct underlying the termination.
Correspondence from both parties can establish the surrounding dispute and support an inference that the termination was contrary to good faith.
Hardship evidence can document the nature and extent of the consequences of termination for the tenant or family.
Medical and household records can together show health-related hardship and the affected household members.
Housing-search records and household registration can show difficulty obtaining suitable replacement housing for the tenant's household.
Hardship evidence and a property-management statement allow the tenant's hardship to be weighed against the landlord's stated interests.
Hardship evidence and landlord correspondence allow comparison of the hardship with the landlord's asserted reasons for termination.
Hardship evidence can establish that ending the tenancy would cause hardship to the tenant or family.
Medical and household records can jointly establish hardship affecting the tenant or the tenant's family.
Housing-search records and household registration can establish hardship arising from the inability to find suitable replacement housing for the household.
These documents allow the tenant's hardship to be compared with the landlord's stated interests in determining whether those interests justify it.
These documents allow the tenant's hardship to be compared with the landlord's asserted termination reasons in determining whether the hardship is justified.
Correspondence exchanged when the lease was made can document the surrounding circumstances and parties' representations at conclusion.
The lease contract records the agreed contractual terms and content.
The lease contract ordinarily states the commencement date and fixed or indefinite duration of the tenancy.
These documents can collectively substantiate the parties' relevant personal, family, medical, and economic circumstances.
Party correspondence together with supporting hardship evidence can show the personal, family, and economic circumstances asserted by both parties.
The parties' correspondence can evidence their respective conduct during the tenancy and dispute.
Payment records and reminders, read with the parties' correspondence, can establish payment-related and other relevant conduct by each party.
Landlord correspondence can state the claimed own-use need and identify the landlord, relative, or relative by marriage for whom the premises are required.
Landlord correspondence can explain the timing and urgency of the asserted own-use need.
Records of searches for replacement premises can evidence availability, pricing, and other conditions in the relevant local premises market.
An authorisation to sue issued after conciliation can establish that the authority conducted or attempted reconciliation between the parties.
The request identifies the tenancy dispute submitted for conciliation, while the authorisation to sue evidences the resulting conciliation process and failure to reach agreement.
The conciliation request can show the application-receipt triggering date, and the authorisation to sue can show the hearing or completion date needed to assess the two-month period.
The conciliation authority's authorisation to sue can record the date on which it received the conciliation application.
Correspondence from both parties can together show offer, acceptance, and the terms of an agreement.
Correspondence from both parties can together show offer, acceptance, and the terms of an agreement.
Correspondence from both parties can together show offer, acceptance, and the terms of an agreement.
A property management statement can record arrears or another recorded default by the claimant.
The conciliation authorisation to sue records the outcome of the conciliation matter, including whether an agreement was reached.
The conciliation authorisation to sue identifies the basis or category under which it was issued.
The lease contract establishes that the dispute arises from a lease relationship and identifies its type.
The conciliation request can identify the subject matter of the dispute, including termination protection or lease extension.
